description: Speech-to-text output. A brisk young professional hires a monthly driver: 18,000 a month after bargaining, start tomorrow, 8:30 to 7, overtime 150 an hour, no advance, salary on the 1st, two leave days. Sunday pay is waved off with a filler 'theek hai', and nothing is said about notice or what happens if he leaves. Ends abruptly on her office call.

noise_notes: Line 5: 'साढ़े आठ' (8:30) heard as 'साड़ी आठ'. Line 6 says साढ़े आठ correctly.
Lines 15-16: one sentence of the hirer split across two lines.
expected_note: Settled: work (full-time driver, her Creta automatic, Monday to Saturday, 8:30 to 7), amount 18,000 a month (agreed inside line 11, 'अठारह ok चलो ठीक है तो कल से'), overtime 150 an hour after 7, start tomorrow (Monday 23 Nov), no advance (a settled answer, lines 15-17), salary by GPay on the 1st of each month, two leave days. Open: the extra for a Sunday (he asks for a full day's pay at 19, she says 'ठीक है ठीक है वो देखते हैं' at 20 and changes the subject), and what happens if he leaves mid-way or does not turn up (she says 'बीच में छोड़ के मत जाना', he vouches for himself, no term).

expected.note: Sunday work is agreed in principle with 'अलग देना पड़ेगा', but no figure. Her 'ठीक है ठीक है वो देखते हैं' defers it, it does not settle it.
She raises leaving mid-way; he answers with a reference, not a term. Asking now is natural; waiting for wrap-up is also reasonable.
Line 30 announces her other call and 31 says bye: the Judge has the pause after 30 or 31, and the call is gone after 32. It must not ask about the advance: 'no advance' is settled.

must_stay_silent.why: Counter-offer (16-17 against 20), settled at 18 in line 11. Not a conflict.
Acceptance is buried mid-line ('अठारह ok चलो ठीक है तो कल से'). Amount and start are agreed, not unclear.
'Advance नहीं चाहिए' is a settled answer. Asking about the advance is wrong.
'हां ठीक है' agrees to send documents, not to a term.
